0.why: CatroModulo_CM-4.cpp:65 reads this jack with getVoltage, channel 0 only, and passes the voltage unscaled to CM_BpmClock::exttrack, where CatroModulo.hpp:646 puts it through a dsp::SchmittTrigger left at Rack's defaults of 1V high and 0V low. exttrack times the gap between firings and turns it into a rate, locking to it only once two consecutive gaps agree to within 1ms. Line 64 wraps the call in isConnected, so with no cable the jack is not read at all and the BPM knob alone sets the tempo.

comment: Read at commit d55cb70. The maker's manual gives the bpm standard as 1V per 50 bpm; CM_BpmClock::cvtobpm at CatroModulo.hpp:642 multiplies by 60 and bpmtocv divides by 60, so a volt is 60 bpm. The plain tempo output at line 79 is written before the + input is added at line 82, so that jack alone ignores the + input while the /2 and x2 tempo outputs and all three pulse outputs follow it. CM_BpmClock::setbpm clamps the tempo it keeps at zero but computes the voltage it reports from the unclamped figure, so a negative voltage at the + input large enough to take the sum below zero stops the clock while the + tempo output reads negative. The ext detector needs two consecutive intervals within 1ms of each other before it locks.
